payload.name: SearchEventMemoriesForSocialConnectionsBesides
payload.description: When a question asks whether someone has friends, teammates, or other social connections besides/apart from a named person, search event memories for team/group activities before concluding no.
content: When a question asks whether someone has friends, teammates, or other social connections 'besides', 'apart from', or 'other than' a named person, do not restrict retrieval to relationship memories or build the query only around 'friend' and the excluded person.

Broaden memory_kinds to include event (and profile/preference when relevant) and run searches with group-activity terms such as team, teammate, club, group, member, tournament, competition, class, coworker, together, plus the person's known activity context.

Inspect any returned event/activity memories for participation that implies other people (e.g., winning a team tournament, joining a club); such memories are valid evidence of social connections beyond the named person.
Before answering 'no' or 'only the named person', discard results that are only about the excluded person and, if no group-activity evidence appeared, try additional expansions.

solves: Diagnosed cause: retrieval was restricted to relationship memories and queries dominated by 'friend' plus the excluded person, so an event memory of the person winning a team tournament was missed even though it implies teammates. The abstract failure is treating social-proof questions as needing explicit relationship records, when group or team events are often the only evidence of additional social ties. This rule applies to any future 'does X have friends/connections besides Y' question across topics.
